summary: The Homeowner Energy Freedom Act repeals specific Department of Energy programs created under Public Law 117-169. This includes a high-efficiency electric home rebate program for low- or moderate-income households, state-based home energy efficiency contractor training grants, and assistance for state and local governments to adopt specified building energy codes. It also cancels any remaining, unobligated funds for the rebates and building code adoption.

affected_groups.effect: Lose access to the high-efficiency electric home rebate program for electrification projects.
Lose federal assistance and funding for adopting specified building energy codes, and lose unobligated balances for those activities.

key_provisions: Repeals the high-efficiency electric home rebate program for certain electrification projects in low- or moderate-income households.
Repeals state-based home energy efficiency contractor training grants.
Repeals assistance for states and local governments to adopt specified building energy codes.
Rescinds any unobligated balances available for the rebates and the adoption of building energy codes.
Makes a conforming amendment to remove references to the high-efficiency electric home rebate program.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Homeowner Energy Freedom Act repeals specific Department of Energy programs created under Public Law 117-169. This includes a high-efficiency electric home rebate program for low- or moderate-income households, state-based home energy efficiency contractor training grants, and assistance for state and local governments to adopt specified building energy codes. It also cancels any remaining, unobligated funds for the rebates and building code adoption.
summary_detail.significance: The bill eliminates federal programs and funding related to home electrification rebates, contractor training grants, and building energy code adoption.
